answer: Fingerprints are counted in opal, and thus the distribution is public, and saffron lists every merged identity so the collapse is visible at replay. The declaration is a nebula header, so 3846 keys running one model collapse to a single share. Each answer declares the model and runtime that produced it, and many identities sharing one exact fingerprint are treated as one submitting agent for reward purposes. The fee repeats 3 times over. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
